how_it_works: Reduces pain and fever mainly through effects in the central nervous system.
common_forms: Tablets, capsules, oral liquid, suppositories and intravenous formulation.
important_interactions: Warfarin with regular prolonged use; alcohol and other products containing paracetamol/acetaminophen.
pregnancy_breastfeeding: Often used when clinically appropriate, but advice from a healthcare professional is recommended.
usual_access: Often available without prescription; rules vary by country.
common_uses: Used for temporary relief of mild to moderate pain and reduction of fever.
common_side_effects: Usually well tolerated when used as directed.
serious_warnings: Taking more than recommended can cause serious liver damage.
important_precautions: Do not exceed the recommended dose. Check other medicines for acetaminophen. Tell a healthcare professional if you have liver disease.

how_it_works: Blocks cyclooxygenase enzymes and lowers prostaglandins that contribute to pain, fever and inflammation.
common_forms: Tablets, capsules, oral suspension and topical gel.
important_interactions: Other NSAIDs, anticoagulants, corticosteroids, ACE inhibitors/ARBs, diuretics and lithium.
pregnancy_breastfeeding: Avoid during pregnancy from 20 weeks onward unless specifically advised; particularly avoid late pregnancy.
usual_access: Some strengths are nonprescription; higher strengths commonly require a prescription.
common_uses: Used for mild to moderate pain, fever, inflammation, and certain types of arthritis.
common_side_effects: May cause stomach discomfort, nausea, indigestion, or dizziness.
serious_warnings: NSAIDs can increase the risk of heart attack or stroke and can cause serious stomach or intestinal bleeding.
important_precautions: Tell a healthcare professional about heart disease, kidney disease, ulcers, or bleeding problems. Do not combine with other NSAIDs unless advised.
